empirical_parent.rule: Theory must explain the empirical evidence ladder without changing the frozen simulation results.

objects.world: w=(A_w,B_w,M_w,tau_w,theta_w), where A,B,M are subsets of X, tau is movement first-arrival state, and theta may contain parameter labels
objects.bam_state_equivalence: w~v iff A_w=A_v, B_w=B_v, M_w=M_v, and tau_w=tau_v

evidence_levels.E0: complete positive occurrence set G* only
evidence_levels.E1: complete presence/absence map: positives G*, negatives X\G*

theorem_targets.corollary: Any positive-superset world with G*⊆G_w is impossible to falsify using positive occurrences alone, even under complete sampling of G*.
Complete perfect presence/absence identifies the realised distribution G but not necessarily its A/B/M decomposition.

theorem_targets.statement: Each later evidence level intersects the previous survivor set with equality constraints on the newly observed state component: tau|G*, A, B, M, then full tau.
S6(w*) equals the exact BAM-state equivalence class [w*]; parameter aliases with identical A,B,M,tau cannot be separated by any E0-E6 evidence.
BAM-state identification at an evidence level occurs iff all surviving worlds belong to one BAM-state equivalence class.

Given a current survivor set S and target fiber T⊆S, a set of direct measurements identifies T iff it hits the disagreement set of every candidate in S\T; the minimum diagnostic design is a finite hitting-set problem.

implementation_checks: construct survivor sets from pure finite-set state objects independent of simulation generator
verify T1-T6 exhaustively for every pair of worlds in small finite universes
verify exact diagnostic hitting-set solver against brute-force subset enumeration on small fixtures
compare exact diagnostic counts with the existing greedy targeted designs; do not call greedy counts minimal unless equality is verified
claim_boundary: The theorems are conditional on the declared finite candidate universe and evidence semantics.
They do not prove that real ecological A, B, M or tau are perfectly observable.
They do not imply that a surviving world is historical truth.
They establish information/identifiability limits, not causal identification from occurrence data.
